blocks.text:
Wes Streeting says deal will ‘get our subs out of the docks and into the sea faster’ amid scrutiny of nuclear deterrent

  • UK politics live – latest updates

  • Business live – latest updates

The Ministry of Defence has signed an £8.7bn contract with defence company Babcock to maintain Britain’s submarine fleet amid scrutiny of the performance of the country’s nuclear deterrent.

The defence secretary, Wes Streeting, said the five-year contract will “get our subs out of the docks and into the sea faster”.
